beat: Continuity of government and federal relocation (COG/COOP, Federal Relocation Arc, FEMA/DCPA/OCD regional centres, Presidential Emergency Facilities, departmental emergency relocation sites)
method_notes: RETRIEVAL STATE, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT GOVERNS EVERYTHING BELOW. WebFetch is blocked for every host I attempted, without exception: clui.org, en.wikipedia.org, coldwar-ct.com, www.orau.org, gao.justia.com, coldwar-c4i.net, www.globalsecurity.org. The repository's research/egress-allowlist.txt lists 118 hosts including en.wikipedia.org, coldwar-c4i.net, globalsecurity.org, apps.dtic.mil, www.gao.gov and www.archives.gov, but that allowlist is NOT live: I tested allowlisted non-.gov hosts (coldwar-c4i.net, globalsecurity.org, en.wikipedia.org) and all three returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. `curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` shows selective=false with an empty recentRelayFailures list, i.e. a blanket proxy posture rather than per-tool scoping. CONSEQUENCE UNDER BES v0.2: I did not open a single document in this sweep. Every observation below derives from WebSearch result titles, URLs and the search tool's own prose summaries of pages it retrieved on my behalf. I have evidence that summaries exist; I do not have evidence of any document's contents. Per BES 2.2 the correct receipt state for every row is UNRESOLVED-UNREACHABLE (network failure, explicitly NOT measured fabrication) and every row is therefore tier V0 and arithmetically inert. Per BES 7.1 the canonical corpora for this beat (CREST, DTIC, NARA Catalog, GovInfo, MILCON J-books, NEPA repositories, GSA disposal, FRPP, county recorders) returned UNSEARCHED, not NEGATIVE. SCI is therefore approximately 0 for every proposition. Per BES 9.4 step 2, with SCI < 0.5 and V empty, EVERY proposition in this file is X — NOT ASSESSED. I have written the band I believe each proposition would reach if its named leads resolved into the `assessment` field, as verification debt under BES 10.5; that conditional is a research target, not a grade, and no proposition here should be published at any band above X. WHAT I SEARCHED. Roughly twenty WebSearch queries across: the OCDM/OCD/DCPA/FEMA regional headquarters programme and each of its eight regional sites; the Presidential Emergency Facility microwave network and its individual code-named sites; the Federal Relocation Arc framing and its numerical claims; departmental emergency relocation sites outside the DC arc; the Raven Rock and Greenbrier anchors for calibration; and backward-tracing queries aimed at the origin of the Mount Weather 'underground city' claim and of the post-2022 bunker-listicle corpus. WHAT WORKED. Searching for the ADMINISTRATIVE STRUCTURE rather than for bunkers was by far the highest-yield technique and it is the one I would repeat. The query that produced the single most valuable result of the sweep asked about the Defense Civil Preparedness Agency's regional office locations and renumbering, not about any facility: it returned a fully enumerated, dated, eight-member list of regional headquarters with their moves (Region 1 Harvard MA 1958-69 then Maynard MA; Region 2 Olney MD; Region 3 Thomasville GA; Region 4 Battle Creek MI; Region 5 Denton TX; Region 6 Denver CO; Region 7 Santa Rosa CA; Region 8 Everett WA 1958-69 then Bothell WA), attributed to the NARA Guide to Federal Records for RG 397 / RG 304. That is a closed candidate set with a hard denominator, arriving from a finding aid rather than from an enthusiast list, and it is exactly the index-enumeration discovery mode BES 5.8(a) prescribes over model-prior-driven searching. Two further techniques paid off: querying historic-preservation channels rather than defence channels surfaced Building 710 at the Denver Federal Center as an NRHP-listed property with a State Historic Preservation Office record, which is the strongest documentary anchor in this beat and has essentially no popular bunker profile; and querying for the COVER STORY rather than the facility surfaced the Front Royal, Virginia State Department relocation site operating under USDA beef-cattle-research-station cover, which is the best novel find here. WHAT WAS BLOCKED. Everything. Specifically blocked and therefore recorded as UNSEARCHED rather than negative: the NARA Guide to Federal Records pages for RG 304, 396, 397 and 311 that are the apparent source of the eight-region enumeration; the ERDC-CERL Phase I archaeological survey of Raven Rock Mountain Complex Site C, whose DTIC accession AD1078617 I saw only as a string inside a search-result URL and did not resolve; the FEMA/ORAU civil defence history PDF (cdhistory.pdf) that would carry the regional-centre construction programme; the GAO civil defence reports NSIAD-84-11, NSIAD-88-52 and LCD-76-464; the NRHP nomination for Building 710; the Smithsonian Institution Archives record on the Front Royal land transfer; and the FRASER finding aid for Federal Reserve Record Group 82 Boston Box 2644 that bears on the Notch currency claim. Each of those is a named, machine-resolvable acquisition target with a known path, and each would be R-SURROGATE or better on a working network. WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH. (1) The size of the regional-centre programme. Three mutually inconsistent counts circulate and I could not adjudicate any of them: 'close to a dozen' regional centres (CLUI), 'six similar operations centers' (Bothell local press), and 'all eight of its regions' (the OCDM planning framing). The eight-region administrative list is well-formed; whether all eight received a purpose-built hardened structure is a different proposition and I have direct construction evidence for only some. (2) Whether Kansas City, Missouri ever held a hardened regional centre. It appears in one compiler's list of built centres but is absent from the eight-region enumeration, and FEMA Region 7's Kansas City office resolves to an ordinary street address. I have left this as an open candidate-set boundary problem rather than calling it either way. (3) Any interior condition, dimension or hardening specification anywhere in this file. Every figure quoted — 37,734 sq ft at Thomasville, 36,000 sq ft at Denver, 120x140 ft and 450 tons of steel at Bothell, one megaton at one mile at Denton, $1.86M and $2.7M construction costs — reached me through a search summary and none is receipted. (4) Whether the Front Royal, Corkscrew or Notch claims survive contact with their primaries. (5) The origin of the '75 Presidential Emergency Facilities among the 90 or so Federal Relocation Arc sites' figure, which is attributed only to unnamed 'former government employees' and which contradicts the separately circulating 'nine PEFs within a 25-minute helicopter trip' figure by a factor of eight. AGENT-INDEPENDENCE DISCLAIMER, PER BES 5.0. I am one agent over one model family searching one indexed web. Nothing in this file is corroborated by the fact that I found it, and if another agent on this fleet returns any of these claims that is the same source found twice, not a second witness. My fan-out value here is recall only.

propositions.statement: Building 710 was engineered to survive the effects of nuclear attack beyond ordinary construction for a 1960s federal office building.
propositions.assessment: Search summaries attribute to GSA and History Colorado the statements that the building was 'designed specifically to withstand a nuclear attack' and 'constructed of reinforced concrete, except for interior partition walls', and was 'designed and constructed by the United States Army Corps of Engineers'. If GSA's own page says that, GSA is the custodial agency and has authority over the fact for its own building, which would be a BES 3.4 gate candidate. I have not seen the page. Note also that 'reinforced concrete with metal-stud partitions' is not by itself a hardening specification — it describes most institutional construction of the period — and no overpressure rating, blast-door specification or design standard reached me. Verification debt: A if the GSA/NRHP text states protective engineering on its face; B if it asserts survivability without specification.

propositions.statement: The structure served as the Defense Civil Preparedness Agency Region 6 emergency operations centre and subsequently as the FEMA Region 8 operations centre.
propositions.assessment: The function is carried in the building's own registered historic name, which is a strong form of claim-property evidence because a naming authority recorded the function for its own unrelated purpose. It also fits the independently arriving eight-region administrative enumeration, in which Denver is Region 6 under OCDM/OCD/DCPA. The renumbering to FEMA Region 8 in 1979 is a real trap: 'Region 6' in a pre-1979 document and 'Region 6' in a post-1979 document are different places (post-1979 Region 6 is Denton, Texas), and any register entry that merges them on the region number alone is committing an entity-resolution error.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A08 — an ordinary earth-bermed or partially below-grade federal office building of late-1960s design on a large federal campus, whose Cold War name reflects the agency that happened to occupy it rather than any protective engineering. This null is genuinely strong: the Denver Federal Center is a sprawling multi-building campus assembled from a wartime ordnance plant, and it contains a great deal of unremarkable government construction. What would distinguish it: the NRHP nomination's statement of significance, or the USACE design record, specifying a design overpressure, blast closures, shielding or CBR filtration. What would NOT distinguish it: earth cover, reinforced concrete, absence of windows, a generator, or the building's Cold War-era name.
candidates.claim_origin: Not a folklore claim and there is no fringe origin to trace — this is an administratively named federal property. The earliest traceable appearance in the material reaching me is institutional rather than popular: the National Register listing dated 16 December 1999, which would have been preceded by a nomination prepared by or for the property's federal custodian. Popular circulation appears to postdate and derive from that institutional record and from the Center for Land Use Interpretation's early-2000s survey, not the reverse. This is the inverse of the usual pattern in this register and it is why the candidate is worth prioritising.
candidates.expected_records: For a 1969 USACE-designed facility on a federal campus for an appropriated civil-defence agency, the records that SHOULD exist are: a construction appropriation or MILCON-equivalent line (X3 for an appropriated agency in this era); USACE design and as-built drawings in RG 77 (X1, flagged ARCHIVE-GAP — roughly 96% of NARA textual holdings are undigitised); a GSA real-property record (X2); and the NRHP nomination form (X3 — NRHP nominations for non-restricted properties are systematically public and their absence WOULD be surprising). The NRHP nomination is the single most valuable expected record here precisely because its absence would be informative, which is rare in this beat. All returned UNSEARCHED, not NEGATIVE.
candidates.lineage_note: Two apparently distinct origins that may not be distinct: the federal historic-preservation record (GSA page, History Colorado record, Lakewood NRHP list) and the enthusiast/curatorial survey (CLUI, virtualglobetrotting). The second almost certainly descends from the first — CLUI's method is to work from public property records — so under the BES 5.1.7 access test and the default-SAME rule these are ONE lineage until a citation graph is actually built. The Lakewood municipal PDF and the History Colorado record may also both descend from the single NRHP nomination, collapsing further. I am not counting lineages here; I am flagging that the apparent breadth is probably illusory.
candidates.confidence_note: Highest-priority candidate in this beat, and the one I would verify first. Reason: it is the only entry here whose decisive document is a public, indexed, machine-resolvable form (an NRHP nomination) rather than a classified or undigitised record. It is therefore the cheapest possible test of whether this beat can produce a band-A proposition at all. If the register cannot verify Building 710, it cannot verify anything on this beat.

propositions.statement: The facility was engineered against nuclear blast effects, including a rated blast door and a stated design overpressure.
propositions.assessment: This is the most specific hardening claim reaching me anywhere on this beat: a 13-ton blast door, air scrubbers, and a design criterion stated as surviving a one-megaton detonation at one mile. A stated design criterion is qualitatively different from 'hardened' as an adjective and is the kind of assertion that traces to an engineering document. But it reached me through popular journalism and a county history blog, not through the engineering record, and a figure of this shape is exactly the sort that propagates unchanged across copies while losing its provenance. The 13-ton door is a physical object a visitor can see and describe; the one-megaton-at-one-mile figure is not, and the two should not be graded together.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A10 — a federal office building whose below-grade levels carry a civil-defence fallout-shelter designation and nothing more, with 'bunker' being a local honorific applied to an ordinary basement. This null is weakened, though not excluded, by the 13-ton door: fallout-shelter designation required shielding mass, not blast closures, and licensed shelter space in ordinary basements was enormously common. What would distinguish it: the door's engineering rating, or an OCD construction contract as opposed to an OCD shelter-survey licence. The civildefensemuseum.com virtual tour appears to be independent of both and works from period civil-defence material.
candidates.expected_records: For 1964 construction by an appropriated civil-defence agency: an appropriation or construction line (X3 — its absence WOULD be surprising for this agency and era); GSA real-property and, latterly, FRPP entries (X2); a Denton County deed for the parcel (X3, the universal floor); USACE or agency design records (X1, ARCHIVE-GAP); local building permits (X0 — federal construction on federal land does not permit locally). Chronicling America coverage of 1964 local press is X0 because the free corpus is copyright-bounded after 1963, which is an unlucky boundary for exactly this facility and pushes the local-press check to newspapers.com or NewsBank. propositions.statement: Federal buildings at the Front Royal property were equipped and stocked as a Department of State emergency relocation site.
propositions.assessment: The reported particulars are unusually mundane and therefore unusually credible in character: office space equipped for the Secretary and a reported 700 State Department employees, a stockpile including a reported 200 typewriters and 10,000 sheets of paper, and regional highway improvements undertaken to support evacuation. Nobody fabricating a bunker story invents a typewriter inventory. That said, character is not evidence, the figures reached me through a popular-history channel, and I have resolved none of it. Note carefully that this proposition is about EQUIPPED BUILDINGS, not about a hardened structure — see HRDN below, which I expect to go the other way.

NOT discriminating: the buildings, the acreage, the federal ownership, the distance from Washington, all of which the agricultural station produces on its own.

propositions.statement: The Front Royal relocation site was hardened against attack effects.
propositions.assessment: I assess this as probably FALSE and I state that plainly rather than leaving it unaddressed. Everything reaching me describes equipped surface buildings on a working agricultural research station — offices, stockpiles, a communications station — and nothing describes a subsurface or protected structure. Under the Federal Relocation Arc's own reported three-layer architecture, the outer 'C team' layer was the LEAST survivable of the three, which is consistent with dispersal-and-continuity rather than blast protection. A relocation site is not necessarily a bunker, and this register should be able to hold that distinction.

FUNCTION(COG relocation) and HARDEN are independent propositions and this site plausibly separates them cleanly — a genuine, documented, federal continuity site that was almost certainly not hardened at all. A register that cannot publish 'real COG function, no hardening' has collapsed two different facts into one.

But note the alternative reading that no source reaching me excludes: the USDA research station may have been entirely genuine — it published research, it had named scientists, its termination in June 1973 is reported as a research-programme decision — and the State Department may simply have been a co-located tenant on a convenient federal parcel. 'Cover' and 'co-location' are very different claims and the sources reaching me do not distinguish them.

Note the calibration parallel and the difference: at the Greenbrier, Forsythe Associates was a shell with no independent purpose; at Front Royal, the cover organisation was doing real science.

candidates.mundane_alternative: A08/A06 — a genuine USDA agricultural research station and former cavalry remount depot, on which the State Department was an ordinary co-located federal tenant occupying some surface buildings for contingency office space, with no concealment and no hardening. What would distinguish the concealment reading: a State Department, GSA or interagency record describing the arrangement, or an emergency-relocation designation document naming the site. What would NOT distinguish it: federal ownership, remoteness, distance from Washington, the presence of a radio station, or the site's later Smithsonian use.
candidates.claim_origin: This is the one candidate in my set where I could NOT trace the claim to a satisfying origin and I want that recorded as a limitation rather than papered over. The circulating account appears in a popular-geography channel (Atlas Obscura) and in the Federal Relocation Arc wiki article, and the specific colourful details — 200 typewriters, 10,000 sheets of paper — have the texture of something quoted from a declassified inventory or from a specific secondary work, but no source reaching me names that parent. Finding it is the first task on this candidate. Until it is found, the whole entry rests on an untraced lineage however plausible it reads, and plausibility is precisely what this register is built not to credit.
candidates.expected_records: State Department emergency-relocation planning records X1 to X2 depending on classification posture; USDA property and programme records for the research station X3, since the agricultural side was entirely unclassified and well-published; Warren County deeds for the parcel X3, the universal floor; the Smithsonian transfer record X3, since Smithsonian acquisitions are institutionally documented and the SI Archives record I saw is exactly this class; General Records Schedule material on federal emergency relocation X1. The USDA and Smithsonian channels are the strong ones and neither is classified — the unclassified half of a concealed arrangement is often the way in, which is a generalisable technique.

The colourful stockpile details appear only in the latter. The USDA research publications and the Smithsonian Institution Archives record are genuinely independent of both, but they attest the AGRICULTURAL and PROPERTY facts, not the continuity claim — which is the classic configuration in which real records get read as corroborating an adjacent claim they do not touch.

It is valuable precisely because it is NOT a bunker: it tests whether the register can hold a documented continuity function apart from a hardening claim, and whether it can resist crediting genuine USDA and Smithsonian records to a State Department proposition they say nothing about.

A self-published blog satisfies none of the custody conditions as it stands, however genuine the author. The architectural detail — pie-shaped rooms in an annulus around a tower base — is distinctive and internally coherent, which is a mild positive signal and also exactly what makes the claim propagate.

The calibration suite's demand that the place-derived contribution to Raven Rock's FUNCTION be exactly zero is the same rule.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: 'The 170 Bunkers They Don't Want You to Know About' — a claimed enumeration of exactly 170 underground and undersea bunkers funded through government spending, some large enough to house tens of thousands indefinitely.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: An article dated 29 July 2026 on theburningplatform.com, encountered while searching for the origin of the 'Federal Relocation Arc' framing. The article asserts its own basis as 'declassified U.S. government documents, testimonies from former federal employees with top-level security clearances, and investigative journalism spanning over two years'.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The self-description is the entire evidentiary content, which is the self-attestation pattern BES 2.5 exists to exclude: the artifact's probative content IS the claim, so it is not a member of V and is evidence only for ORIGIN. Not one document identifier, accession number, appropriation line or facility name accompanies the count in anything reaching me — and a claim of the form 'exactly 170' is a claim that necessarily rests on an enumeration, so the absence of the enumeration is not incidental but disqualifying. The witnesses are unnamed and therefore fail the BES 5.4 resolvability gate at the first clause. The item is post-2022 with no byline reaching me, which under BES 3.3 makes it POST-2022-UNATTRIBUTED, contributing zero to every condition and counting as zero lineages by construction. Note what I am NOT saying: I am not asserting that no such document set exists. I am recording that this artifact provides no path to one.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A traffic-driven aggregation article assembling publicly known facilities — Mount Weather, Cheyenne Mountain, the FEMA regional centres — into a round-numbered list, with the specificity of '170' supplying an authority the underlying material does not have. Every named facility I could see in it is one that appears in ordinary public sources.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: FEMA regional centres are 'regional nodes' of a covert deep-underground network, as presented in state-by-state 'list of DUMBs' pages.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A cluster of undated or 2026-dated pages including coreinsightsintl.com 'List of DUMBs by State', subterraneanbases.com state pages (e.g. 'Georgia Underground Bases: 2026 Intelligence & FEMA Regional Nodes', 'Washington Underground: Mel's Hole & Madigan Grey Nest Vaults'), and deepundergroundmilitarybases.com. All surfaced incidentally while searching for the legitimate Federal Regional Centers.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: These pages take real, named, publicly acknowledged federal facilities with published addresses — the FEMA regional operations centres at Denton, Thomasville, Bothell, Denver and Maynard — and re-present them as concealed installations, adding no identifier, record or observation to the public material they restyle. The tell is structural and checkable: the genuine content is exactly the set of facilities already documented by the Center for Land Use Interpretation and by local journalism, while the added content ('Grey Nest Vaults') attaches to nothing at all. The lineage is the Sauder/Schneider deep-underground-military-base corpus, which this project's calibration suite grades F with V empty on the ground that the originator is the claimant and the content is the claim. Titles carrying a future-dated '2026 Intelligence' framing with no byline are POST-2022-UNATTRIBUTED under BES 3.3.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Search-engine-optimised aggregation over a fringe corpus. The FEMA regional centres are real, hardened in several cases, and entirely acknowledged — they are listed on FEMA's own site, one is on the National Register of Historic Places, and journalists have filmed inside one. Nothing is being concealed, which is why the pages can be assembled from public sources in the first place.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Mount Weather contains an underground city with streets, sidewalks, a battery-powered subway, a lake fed by underground springs, hydroponic gardens and residential apartments.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Traced, and it terminates cleanly. Richard Pollock, 'The Mysterious Mountain', The Progressive, March 1976, based on Senate subcommittee material plus several off-the-record interviews with officials formerly associated with the facility. Every circulating version reaching me descends from it.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Hollow as EVIDENCE, not necessarily false as fact, and the distinction matters. Pollock is a journalist reporting others' attestation rather than the claimant, so BES 2.5 does not exclude him — his report enters V at the D0 unresolvable-attestation floor. The witnesses are unnamed and fail the resolvability gate at its first clause. The result is the citogenesis pattern the model is built to name: a T3 publication resting on T5 testimony, subsequently cited as though primary across some hundreds of pages. I counted eight downstream carriers in a single result set (allconspiracy, moraloutrage, humansarefree, beforeitsnews, usahitman, conspiracybomb, a dedicated blogspot, a Goodreads thread) and every one of them is a copy: that is ONE lineage at any volume. This project's calibration suite grades the claim E with a citogenesis flag, and requires the flag to attach to the PROPOSITION rather than to the site.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Mount Weather is a genuine, acknowledged, federally operated facility whose existence is graded A in this project's own calibration set — a 434-acre site with tunnels begun in 1954 under the Bureau of Mines and completed by the Army Corps of Engineers, with a reported 200,000 sq ft of built space. A large real facility with a sewage plant, water storage and dormitory capacity for a few hundred people is entirely sufficient to generate 'underground city' language when described second-hand by people who were inside it and are speaking without attribution. The site's A-grade existence and the claim's E-grade status belong on the same page without contradiction.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: There were 75 Presidential Emergency Facilities among the 90 or so Federal Relocation Arc sites.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Attributed in the material reaching me only to 'former government employees', appearing in the Federal Relocation Arc wiki article and its derivatives. I could not trace it further and I record that failure.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: It contradicts by a factor of roughly eight the separately circulating and better-anchored figure that in 1984 there were NINE Presidential Emergency Facilities within a 25-minute helicopter trip of Washington, and it sits uneasily beside a third framing describing 'seven locations that would become the core PEFs'. The nine-and-seven figures are reconcilable as core-versus-expanded counts; 75 is not reconcilable with either. The attribution is to unnamed persons and therefore fails the BES 5.4 resolvability gate outright, and under the attestation-custody rule the lineage terminus is the anonymous asserter, not the officials invoked. Note the specific danger: this is a number that would, if credited, silently multiply the candidate-set denominator M in the BES C1c rule and thereby change the grade of every individual arc-site candidate in the register. A single untraced number with no custody must not be allowed to do that.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Probable conflation of two different populations that the sources do not keep apart: the small set of purpose-built PRESIDENTIAL emergency facilities in the immediate Washington region, and the much larger set of roughly 90 departmental EMERGENCY RELOCATION SITES across the 30-to-300-mile arc — of which Front Royal, in this file, is one. Those are different things with different builders, different protection levels and different orders of magnitude, and reading the second population's count into the first produces exactly this error.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: A hardened Federal Regional Center bunker was built at Kansas City, Missouri.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Appears in the Center for Land Use Interpretation's list of locations where regional centres were built ('Maynard MA, Denton TX, Denver CO, Olney MD, Kansas City MO, and Bothell WA'), and propagates from there.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: PROVISIONALLY HOLLOW AND EXPLICITLY NOT REFUTED — I am flagging a discrepancy I could not resolve, and I want the uncertainty preserved rather than converted into a finding. Kansas City does not appear in the eight-member OCDM/OCD/DCPA regional-headquarters enumeration (Harvard/Maynard, Olney, Thomasville, Battle Creek, Denton, Denver, Santa Rosa, Everett/Bothell), and targeted searching for a Kansas City federal regional bunker returned nothing describing a hardened structure — only FEMA Region 7's current office at an ordinary street address, plus two genuine but unrelated underground sites in the region (SubTropolis, a commercial limestone mine which this project's calibration suite grades R on the COG proposition, and the Atchison Storage Facility across the state line in Kansas). The most likely reading is that Kansas City entered the list as a post-1979 FEMA REGION headquarters rather than as a pre-1979 purpose-built CENTER, conflating two different things the same list mixes elsewhere. But a compiler as careful as CLUI including it is a real signal and I will not dismiss it on a failed search conducted with no working retrieval.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: FEMA Region 7's Kansas City office is an ordinary leased or owned federal office. The area's genuine large underground spaces are commercial limestone mines with documented commercial tenants — precisely the configuration this project's calibration suite uses as its negative control against real bunkers — and their presence in the same metropolitan area is an obvious route for a regional-centre claim to attach itself to the wrong kind of hole.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The Federal Reserve stored large sums of currency at the Notch (Bare Mountain, Hadley, Massachusetts) to restart the economy after a nuclear war.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Untraced. Appears in wiki-family text about the PACCS facility, hedged in the sources themselves with 'allegedly', with no named source anywhere in the material reaching me.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Carried entirely within a single wiki lineage whose members I saw six of in one result set, so it has ONE source at any apparent volume. Its carriers decline to vouch for it. And a documented alternative referent for the same story exists in the same period: the Federal Reserve's Mount Pony facility at Culpeper, Virginia genuinely held shrink-wrapped currency for post-attack monetary reconstitution from 1969 to 1988, and is a calibration case in this project's own suite. A currency-reconstitution narrative attaching to a second, unrelated Federal Reserve-occupied bunker is the standard shape of a transposition. Recorded as a live transposition hypothesis with a named discriminating test — the FRASER finding aid for Federal Reserve Record Group 82, Boston, Box 2644 — not as an established refutation. The separate and much duller claim that the Fed stored RECORDS there is unremarkable and I have no reason to doubt it.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: The Federal Reserve Bank of Boston used a decommissioned and genuinely hardened SAC command post for records storage, which is exactly what surplus hardened federal space gets used for. 'The Fed kept records in the bunker' becomes 'the Fed kept money in the bunker' in retelling without anyone intending to deceive, especially once the Culpeper story enters general circulation and supplies a template.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: GENERAL FINDING, recorded as hollow because it is a claim about the RECORD rather than about any site: that the apparent breadth of online sourcing on Federal Relocation Arc facilities constitutes corroboration.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Not a claim anyone makes explicitly; it is the implicit premise of every aggregated bunker list, and it is the failure mode this register was built against, so I record it as a finding of the sweep.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Measured directly and repeatedly across this beat. On Warrenton Training Center, six of nine results were Wikipedia derivatives (Military Wiki/Fandom, HandWiki, dbpedia, Grokipedia, plus mirrors) — one lineage presenting as six. On the Notch, six wiki-family members appeared in a single result set. On the Mount Weather 'underground city' claim, eight downstream carriers all descend from Pollock 1976. On the FEMA regional centres, one CLUI sentence about the class ('close to a dozen sophisticated regional centers... several hundred people for 30 days or more') appears verbatim in results for Maynard, Denton and Thomasville alike, and is being read at each as instance evidence when it is CLASS scope and excluded from V under BES 2.4. Under the BES 5.1.7 access test the picture is consistent: the sources that could have observed the underlying facts independently — county recorders, contracting officers, GSA property officers, the Keeper of the National Register, AFHRA, NARA — are almost exactly the set I could not reach, while the sources I could reach are almost exactly the set that copies from one another.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A small number of genuine compilers did real work — the Center for Land Use Interpretation, civildefensemuseum.com, coldwar-c4i.net, a handful of state Cold War documentation projects, and NARA's own record-group guides — and the visible remainder of the web is derivative of them. The correct reading is that this beat has perhaps five to eight genuine secondary termini and a very large number of copies, and that real corroboration on it lives exclusively in institutional records none of which were reachable in this cycle.

coverage_gaps: WHAT I DID NOT COVER, AND WHY. (1) The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island is absent from the candidate list although I searched it and confirmed the anchor facts (Ted Gup, Washington Post, 31 May 1992; construction 1959-62 alongside the West Virginia Wing; the Forsythe Associates cover). It is calibration case B-05/A-05 and I could add nothing to it under snippet-only retrieval. Same for Mount Weather as an entity, though its 'underground city' claim is worked in refuted_or_hollow, and same for Cheyenne Mountain. (2) The remaining PEF sites — Cartwheel at Fort Reno Park in the District of Columbia, Cannonball at Cross Mountain near Mercersburg Pennsylvania, Cowpuncher at Martinsburg West Virginia, Cadre/Creed near Site R, Cactus, and Crystal at Mount Weather — are each identified with a location and a site number but I worked up only Corkscrew. Cartwheel is the most interesting omission because it is calibration case B-03, sits under a public city park, and turns on whether White House Army Signal Agency records name Fort Reno at instance or only at class level. (3) The eight-region enumeration's own source. I saw the list; I never reached the NARA Guide pages for RG 304, 396, 397 or 311 that appear to carry it. Everything structural in this file rests on that unverified list and a downstream process should treat it as a single unresolved lineage, not as a finding aid. (4) Departmental emergency relocation sites beyond Front Royal. If roughly 90 arc sites existed, I have touched one, and the college-campus sites mentioned in passing by the arc literature are entirely unexamined. This is the largest recall gap in the beat and probably the richest remaining seam. (5) State-level emergency operating centres, which are numerous, frequently hardened, and documented in state rather than federal records — an entirely unworked corpus that is also unusually reachable, since state archives and state emergency-management agencies publish. (6) Post-1980s and post-9/11 continuity architecture. I touched Peters Mountain, Albemarle County Virginia — an AT&T troposcatter and long-lines site reported as nuclear-hardened, reported to house several hundred people, and reported to have had a renovation exceeding $61 million since 2007 — but did not develop it, and it is the strongest live COG candidate I did not work up. It also sits at the intersection of this beat and the AT&T Long Lines beat and should be coordinated rather than duplicated. (7) The Federal Preparedness Agency inheritance within GSA (NARA RG 269) was named in my brief and I did not reach it at all. (8) HERT, the Headquarters Emergency Relocation Team, surfaced as a SAC continuity unit at Offutt AFB with a dispersal location at the Cornhusker Army Ammunition Plant, Grand Island, Nebraska, superseded circa 1982 by the Enduring Battle Management Support Center. I excluded it because it is a UNIT rather than a structure and carries no hardened-facility claim, but the dispersal locations it used are unexamined and are exactly the sort of unglamorous COG geography this beat is supposed to find. (9) MOST IMPORTANTLY: no canonical corpus was searched in the BES 7.1 sense. Zero queries against CREST, DTIC, NARA Catalog, GovInfo, the Federal Register, FRUS, GAO, MILCON J-books, NEPA repositories, FRPP, the DoD Base Structure Report, USAspending/FPDS, county recorders or the USGS historical topographic stack. SCI is therefore approximately zero across this entire beat and no negative finding anywhere in this file is a NEGATIVE — every one of them is UNSEARCHED. Nothing here should be read as evidence of absence, and the several places where I say 'I searched for undercutting evidence and found none' should be read as statements about my reach, not about the world.
